reading.body:
Verizon filed five Lobbying Disclosure Act reports naming AI, and sixteen lobbyists appear across them.

The filings name six bills, all from 2025 or later: S 4407, S 3062, S 3813, HR 8516, HR 7757, and HR 7294. Five lobbyists appear on all five filings, and six more appear on four, so a small core carries most of the activity. The remaining five appear once each. That concentration is the pattern: this is a standing account with a stable team, not a one-off push.

For AI specifically, the filings show a telecommunications firm treating AI as a legislative subject rather than a product line. The bills are named but the positions are not, so the data cannot say whether Verizon supports or opposes any of them. What it does show is that AI policy work runs through the same registered lobbying channel as the rest of a large firm's Washington business.

The data does not cover spending, lobbying contacts, or the content of any filing. It also does not connect these filings to data centers, power procurement, or grid policy, even though a firm like Verizon might have interests there. Nothing here supports a claim about compute or electricity. It covers one registrant, one client, and the bills and lobbyists named.

summary: VERIZON COMMUNICATIONS INC. AND VARIOUS SUBSIDIARIES filed 5 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 5836.
